{
  "thinking": "The table is empty and the clock is running. A simple fish outline is easy to draw and easy to recognize, so I'll take the pad and sketch it before anyone starts placing dominoes.",
  "say": "Okay, I'll grab the pad. How about a fish? A simple closed outline with a tail and an eye should read well from across the table. Shout if you'd like a different animal.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 8,
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type":"curve","points":[[8,10],[9,7],[12,5],[16,5],[19,7],[21,9],[26,4]]},
    {"type":"curve","points":[[26,4],[24,10],[26,16]]},
    {"type":"curve","points":[[26,16],[21,11],[19,13],[16,15],[12,15],[9,13],[8,10]]},
    {"type":"label","x":11,"y":9,"text":"eye"}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Plan: fish outline. Stroke 1 starts at the nose (START, about (8,10)), runs over the top to the tail tip (about (26,4)). Stroke 2 comes back from the tail tip to the tail base. Stroke 3 runs along the belly and closes at the nose. Eye at about (11,9). I hold the pad for now."
}

{
  "thinking": "Empty table and the round is starting. I want a simple animal that one clean run can draw. A fish, drawn from the tail, can be traced as one outline with fins off the start.",
  "say": "Right, let's do a fish. The start goes at the tail. We run one line along the top to the nose, back along the bottom, and the tail fins branch off the start. Simple enough to get right in ten minutes.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 7,
  "point": [8, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[8,10],[11,7.5],[16,7],[21,8.5],[24,10],[21,11.5],[16,13],[11,12.5],[8,10]]},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 8, "y0": 10, "x1": 5, "y1": 7},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 8, "y0": 10, "x1": 5, "y1": 13},
    {"type": "circle", "cx": 20.5, "cy": 9.2, "r": 0.5},
    {"type": "label", "x": 8, "y": 9, "text": "START"}
  ],
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Plan: fish. Stroke 1 is the body outline, starting at the tail (START). Fins branch off the tail. Eye at the front. Once the pad is sketched, trace stroke 1 first, then the fins."
}

{
  "thinking": "The table's empty and the clock's running, so I'll propose something easy to build. A fish is simple: one body outline and a tail. I'll take the pad and sketch it so people can see the plan.",
  "say": "Let's do a fish. Big one, nose pointing right, tail on the left. I've put the body outline on the pad. We run the top edge out from the tail, then the bottom edge back round, so both sides meet at the nose.",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 6,
  "point": [15, 10],
  "pad": "take",
  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "label", "x": 8, "y": 10, "text": "START"},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[8, 10], [11, 7.5], [16, 7], [21, 9], [23, 10]]},
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[8, 10], [11, 12.5], [16, 13], [21, 11], [23, 10]]},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 8, "y0": 10, "x1": 3, "y1": 6},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 8, "y0": 10, "x1": 3, "y1": 14}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
  "notes": "Plan: fish facing right. Start at the tail end (left) of the body. Stroke 1 is the top edge, stroke 2 the bottom edge, strokes 3 and 4 the tail fins. Maya/Priya/Leo haven't weighed in yet. I'm holding the pad."
}

  "say": "Quick idea: a little songbird in profile, facing right. I've got the pad and I'm sketching it now. Tail's on the left, so the start goes at the tail tip.",

  "eagerness": 6,
  "point": [6, 9],

  "sketch_clear": true,
  "sketch": [
    {"type": "curve", "points": [[6, 9], [10, 6.5], [15, 6], [19, 6]]},

    {"type": "line", "x0": 13, "y0": 6.2, "x1": 9, "y1": 11},
    {"type": "line", "x0": 21.5, "y0": 7.5, "x1": 23.5, "y1": 8}
  ],
  "do": "continue",
